title: sealed OCI registry connector and ephemeral-registry terraform egress module for RHEL8/k0s airgap installs
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds sealed OCI registry connector and terraform 'airgap-egress' module; RHEL8 signed runtime index; k0s bootstrap support. Opt-in, non-breaking improvements to on-prem installer.
body: Summary: Introduce a sealed-OCI-registry connector component that enables an ephemeral local registry sidecar to serve signed, content-addressable runtime bundles in fully offline sites, plus a small Terraform module (airgap-egress) to provision minimal egress rules/NAT for controlled registry seeding. Motivation: many customers deploy Redwood Private in heavily restricted networks where a full persistent registry is undesirable. The connector provides a deterministic, GPG-signed index and lockfile so site operators can seed an ephemeral registry from a single sealed bundle and safely update it with delta snapshots. This PR also adds explicit RHEL8 slim runtime bundles with sha512 manifests, and lightweight k0s bootstrap shims to broaden supported kube distros. What changed (checklist): [x] sealed OCI registry connector service and operator; [x] terraform/modules/airgap-egress with security-group/NAT template and examples; [x] bundles/rhel8/signed-index and manifest generator; [x] installer/bootstrap/k0s shim and preflight checks; [x] helm chart updates for airgap-registry (values to enable sealed mode); [x] e2e harness for offline seeding smoke test. Design notes: The connector runs as a short-lived job+sidecar pair that validates the sealed bundle's GPG signature, materializes blobs to a local registry, writes an immutable lockfile (content-addressed), and exposes a /prometheus metrics endpoint for seeding progress. The Terraform module creates a minimal 'airgap-egress' security group plus an optional NAT gateway and a route table that can be used in on-prem clouds or private VPC-like environments; the defaults are conservative and require explicit enablement. Backwards compatibility: All features are opt-in. Existing installs will not change behavior unless users enable the new helm value 'airgap.registry.sealed.enabled=true' or apply the terraform module. Testing: Unit tests for manifest/signature verification; integration test that seeds a k0s cluster with the ephemeral registry in an isolated container network; manual verification on RHEL8 VM for package index and systemd unit templates. Operators guide (short): 1) Create sealed bundle using tools/bundle/seal.sh; 2) Apply terraform module to create egress ACLs if you need SRC NAT for registry seeding; 3) Install helm chart with sealed mode enabled and point to the sealed bundle local path or HTTP artifact; 4) Run installer bootstrap (k0s or kubeadm) which invokes preflight that checks lockfile hashes. Links: Linear ENG-2981 (offline registry UX), ENG-3050 (rhel bundles), SUP-1219 (customer request). Related: RFC#2026 (airgap-sealed-bundles). Notes for operators: signed-index uses GPG key rotation via keys stored in the sealed bundle; connector enforces a strict key whitelist. Security: no persistent credentials left on disk, registry blobs are stored under a per-job ephemeral directory and pruned after the seed completes unless 'persist=true' is set in Helm values. Migration plan: None required; opt-in feature. Rollback: Helm value toggle and Terraform destroy for egress module. Known limitations: does not yet support policy-driven delta merges across multiple sealed bundles; larger installs (>10GB) will need longer seeding window and may choose a persistent mirror. Checklist before merge: [x] design review approved; [x] tests green in CI; [x] e2e smoke on k0s green; [x] documentation updated in docs/airgap/sealed-connector.md; [x] security review completed.
